88:{"n":27,"title":"docs: lunR identity for the published npm package","merged":true,"body":"## Summary

User-facing docs for the published npm package `@ashx-j/lunr` (what npmjs shows: `packages/coding-agent` README/docs/examples/CHANGELOG), not the repo-root README.

The shipped docs still described Pi: `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, binary `pi`, `~/.pi/`, `pi.dev/install.sh`, and `pi update --models`. After a global install, lunR’s system prompt points the model at those files.

## What changed

- Install/uninstall: `@ashx-j/lunr`, binary `lunr`, Node ≥ 22.19. No pi.dev curl installer. `lunr uninstall --purge` wipes `~/.lunr/agent`.
- Config: `~/.lunr/agent` and project `.lunr/`. Document `lunr setup` / `lunr features` / `lunr gateway`.
- Catalog refresh is `/refresh`. `lunr update` only reinstalls the global CLI.
- Commands/keys/settings: no `/changelog`; Shift+Tab cycles permission mode; builtin theme is `moon`; lunR settings added; Pi telemetry flags removed.
- New [Built-in features](packages/coding-agent/docs/features.md) page (gateway, cron, MCP/LSP, swarm, plan, SuperGrok, local models).
- SDK install: `npm install @ashx-j/lunr`. Dropped `../src` / `../test` links that 404 after npm install. Dropped stale `files` entry for missing root `containerization.md`.
- CHANGELOG: lunR 0.2.11 note at the top; `0.80.x` left as labeled upstream pi history.

## Intentional pi compatibility (not renamed)

- ExtensionAPI callback parameter `pi`
- package.json resource manifest key `pi`
- `PI_CODING_AGENT_*` / `PI_OFFLINE` / `PI_SHARE_VIEWER_URL` (`/share` still defaults to pi.dev)
- Workspace package names `@earendil-works/pi-*` (publish rewrites to `@ashx-j/lunr*`)
- jiti aliases both names when lunR loads extensions

## Test plan

- [x] `npm pack --dry-run --ignore-scripts --workspace=@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` includes README, `docs/**`, `examples/**`
- [x] Grep shipped markdown: no `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` as an npm install command, no `pi.dev/install.sh`, no `pi update --models` outside labeled CHANGELOG history

90:{"n":25,"title":"fix: eliminate disabled-watchdog cold-start scans","merged":true,"body":"## Summary

- remove eager Git worktree fingerprinting from watchdog construction and session binding
- gate repository signatures on the effective main-watchdog enablement state
- lazily establish the repo-edit baseline at the first relevant `before_agent_start`
- clear signature state across session and disable boundaries
- add regression coverage for disabled startup, enabled change review, pre-existing dirty files, and session rebinding

## Root cause

`MainWatchdogRuntime` computed the complete repository change signature in its constructor, then twice more while binding the initial session. This happened even though the main watchdog is disabled by default. The signature invokes Git status and stats/hashes dirty paths, so Windows cold filesystem, Defender, and OneDrive state could turn deferred subagent attachment into a multi-second first-prompt delay.

The fix removes all constructor/session-bind scans. An enabled repo-edit watchdog now fingerprints once at turn start and once at agent end, preserving the existing rule that only edits made during that turn trigger review.

## Verification

- focused Vitest regression set: 25/25 passed
- required tsgo build sequence passed: tui, ai, agent, coding-agent, orchestrator
- touched-file Biome passed; the vendored watchdog source remains excluded by repository configuration
- dirty-worktree startup benchmark: prompt-ready 2.23s, deferred attach 265ms, `pi-subagents` factory 6ms

The full coding-agent suite was also attempted: 2236 tests passed and 125 failed in unrelated current-master/Windows areas; no watchdog test failed. Full Biome reports 35 existing errors and one warning outside the touched files.

## Out of scope

The larger first-paint ESM/TypeBox module graph remains a secondary cold-cache amplifier. This PR intentionally does not refactor that graph or the startup profiler; it fixes only the experimentally isolated default-off watchdog scan.

113:{"n":2,"title":"feat(agent): agent-swarm approval gate for auto-activated parallel fan-out","merged":false,"body":"## What

An auto-activated agent swarm — one `subagent` tool call launching **more than 2 parallel subagents** — now requires user approval in **manual and yolo** modes. Only `auto` mode bypasses the gate. Explicit `/swarm` turns are pre-approved (the user already asked for the swarm).

TUI dialog:

```
▶ Approve AgentSwarm?

agent swarm (4 subagents)
Explore lunR auth/model/settings/plan systems

  1. Approve once
  2. Approve for this session
  3. Reject
  4. Reject with feedback
```

Reject-with-feedback collects a one-line reason that becomes the block reason the model sees, so it can adjust the plan. On approval the footer shows `swarm ● active` for the rest of the turn, same as an explicit /swarm.

## How

- `core/swarm.ts`: `SWARM_APPROVAL_THRESHOLD` (2), `effectiveSwarmCount` (tasks[] with `count` multipliers + chain `parallel` blocks; dynamic `expand` fan-out has no static count and is not gated), `isExplicitSwarmTurn` (last user message starts with `[SWARM MODE]` — works for TUI + gateway since both inject the same prompt).
- `core/permissions.ts`: swarm branch in `gateToolCall` runs before the mode early-return so yolo is gated too; `ApprovalResponse` is now decision strings OR `{ decision: "reject", feedback }`; `ApprovalRequest.kind?: "swarm"`; session approval under the `"swarm"` action key; fail-closed without a handler.
- `agent-session.ts`: computes `explicitSwarmTurn` from the branch, passes via new `GateOptions`.
- TUI: `showSwarmApprovalDialog`; `ExtensionSelectorComponent` gains 1-9 number-key selection (all selectors).
- Gateway: AgentSwarm prompt title; buttons stay once/session/reject — inline buttons can't capture free text, so reject-with-feedback is TUI-only.

## Verification

- `permissions.test.ts` grew to 26 tests (swarm count helpers, mode matrix, explicit-swarm exemption, session approval, reject-feedback reason, fail-closed) — all pass
- `gateway-approval.test.ts` (6) passes

90:{"n":25,"title":"fix: eliminate disabled-watchdog cold-start scans","merged":true,"body":"## Summary

- remove eager Git worktree fingerprinting from watchdog construction and session binding
- gate repository signatures on the effective main-watchdog enablement state
- lazily establish the repo-edit baseline at the first relevant `before_agent_start`
- clear signature state across session and disable boundaries
- add regression coverage for disabled startup, enabled change review, pre-existing dirty files, and session rebinding

## Root cause

`MainWatchdogRuntime` computed the complete repository change signature in its constructor, then twice more while binding the initial session. This happened even though the main watchdog is disabled by default. The signature invokes Git status and stats/hashes dirty paths, so Windows cold filesystem, Defender, and OneDrive state could turn deferred subagent attachment into a multi-second first-prompt delay.

The fix removes all constructor/session-bind scans. An enabled repo-edit watchdog now fingerprints once at turn start and once at agent end, preserving the existing rule that only edits made during that turn trigger review.

## Verification

- focused Vitest regression set: 25/25 passed
- required tsgo build sequence passed: tui, ai, agent, coding-agent, orchestrator
- touched-file Biome passed; the vendored watchdog source remains excluded by repository configuration
- dirty-worktree startup benchmark: prompt-ready 2.23s, deferred attach 265ms, `pi-subagents` factory 6ms

The full coding-agent suite was also attempted: 2236 tests passed and 125 failed in unrelated current-master/Windows areas; no watchdog test failed. Full Biome reports 35 existing errors and one warning outside the touched files.

## Out of scope

The larger first-paint ESM/TypeBox module graph remains a secondary cold-cache amplifier. This PR intentionally does not refactor that graph or the startup profiler; it fixes only the experimentally isolated default-off watchdog scan.

113:{"n":2,"title":"feat(agent): agent-swarm approval gate for auto-activated parallel fan-out","merged":false,"body":"## What

An auto-activated agent swarm — one `subagent` tool call launching **more than 2 parallel subagents** — now requires user approval in **manual and yolo** modes. Only `auto` mode bypasses the gate. Explicit `/swarm` turns are pre-approved (the user already asked for the swarm).

TUI dialog:

```
▶ Approve AgentSwarm?

agent swarm (4 subagents)
Explore lunR auth/model/settings/plan systems

  1. Approve once
  2. Approve for this session
  3. Reject
  4. Reject with feedback
```

Reject-with-feedback collects a one-line reason that becomes the block reason the model sees, so it can adjust the plan. On approval the footer shows `swarm ● active` for the rest of the turn, same as an explicit /swarm.

## How

- `core/swarm.ts`: `SWARM_APPROVAL_THRESHOLD` (2), `effectiveSwarmCount` (tasks[] with `count` multipliers + chain `parallel` blocks; dynamic `expand` fan-out has no static count and is not gated), `isExplicitSwarmTurn` (last user message starts with `[SWARM MODE]` — works for TUI + gateway since both inject the same prompt).
- `core/permissions.ts`: swarm branch in `gateToolCall` runs before the mode early-return so yolo is gated too; `ApprovalResponse` is now decision strings OR `{ decision: "reject", feedback }`; `ApprovalRequest.kind?: "swarm"`; session approval under the `"swarm"` action key; fail-closed without a handler.
- `agent-session.ts`: computes `explicitSwarmTurn` from the branch, passes via new `GateOptions`.
- TUI: `showSwarmApprovalDialog`; `ExtensionSelectorComponent` gains 1-9 number-key selection (all selectors).
- Gateway: AgentSwarm prompt title; buttons stay once/session/reject — inline buttons can't capture free text, so reject-with-feedback is TUI-only.

## Verification

- `gateway-approval.test.ts` (6) passes

90:{"n":25,"title":"fix: eliminate disabled-watchdog cold-start scans","merged":true,"body":"## Summary

- remove eager Git worktree fingerprinting from watchdog construction and session binding
- gate repository signatures on the effective main-watchdog enablement state
- lazily establish the repo-edit baseline at the first relevant `before_agent_start`
- clear signature state across session and disable boundaries
- add regression coverage for disabled startup, enabled change review, pre-existing dirty files, and session rebinding

## Root cause

`MainWatchdogRuntime` computed the complete repository change signature in its constructor, then twice more while binding the initial session. This happened even though the main watchdog is disabled by default. The signature invokes Git status and stats/hashes dirty paths, so Windows cold filesystem, Defender, and OneDrive state could turn deferred subagent attachment into a multi-second first-prompt delay.

The fix removes all constructor/session-bind scans. An enabled repo-edit watchdog now fingerprints once at turn start and once at agent end, preserving the existing rule that only edits made during that turn trigger review.

## Verification

- focused Vitest regression set: 25/25 passed
- required tsgo build sequence passed: tui, ai, agent, coding-agent, orchestrator
- touched-file Biome passed; the vendored watchdog source remains excluded by repository configuration
- dirty-worktree startup benchmark: prompt-ready 2.23s, deferred attach 265ms, `pi-subagents` factory 6ms

The full coding-agent suite was also attempted: 2236 tests passed and 125 failed in unrelated current-master/Windows areas; no watchdog test failed. Full Biome reports 35 existing errors and one warning outside the touched files.

## Out of scope

The larger first-paint ESM/TypeBox module graph remains a secondary cold-cache amplifier. This PR intentionally does not refactor that graph or the startup profiler; it fixes only the experimentally isolated default-off watchdog scan.

113:{"n":2,"title":"feat(agent): agent-swarm approval gate for auto-activated parallel fan-out","merged":false,"body":"## What

▶ Approve AgentSwarm?

agent swarm (4 subagents)
Explore lunR auth/model/settings/plan systems

  1. Approve once
  2. Approve for this session
  3. Reject
  4. Reject with feedback
```

Reject-with-feedback collects a one-line reason that becomes the block reason the model sees, so it can adjust the plan. On approval the footer shows `swarm ● active` for the rest of the turn, same as an explicit /swarm.

- `agent-session.ts`: computes `explicitSwarmTurn` from the branch, passes via new `GateOptions`.
- TUI: `showSwarmApprovalDialog`; `ExtensionSelectorComponent` gains 1-9 number-key selection (all selectors).

Review pinned to clean `origin/master` at `b57c148`. I made no repository changes. The focused gateway, session, approval, cron, and permission tests passed **328/328**. Packaging fixture tests passed **23/23**, and the lock and publication-policy checks passed.

### Findings

- **Medium, stale gateway notification:** `packages/coding-agent/src/gateway/presenter.ts:81-109,116-118` stores an epoch with each queued notice but never checks it when retrying delivery. I reproduced this with a local fake adapter: the first send failed, the conversation changed, and the retry delivered `"OLD SESSION result"` to the new conversation. No bot or network was used.
- **Low, incorrect shipped path:** `packages/coding-agent/docs/features.md:146` says documents go to `.lunr/uploads/`; `src/gateway/agent-bridge.ts:572` writes them to `.lunr/gateway-uploads/`.
- **Separate pi remnants:** Shipped example instructions still direct users to `~/.pi/agent`, including `examples/sdk/06-extensions.ts:8-9` and `examples/extensions/commands.ts:8`. The documented `pi.dev` default for `/share`, `PI_*` names, and workspace package names are intentional compatibility, not findings.

Scoped disposition: the available fixtures support the gateway and release-package contracts, including PR #96's ownership and handoff logic, but **PR #96 is not fully qualified for live use** until its Telegram/Discord and native startup scenarios are verified. The stale-notification finding needs a fix. The shipped-doc findings warrant correction. I found no failure in the tested lock or publication-policy checks.

No compiled-current package claim is possible: this isolated worktree has no `dist`, and linked workspace dependencies may resolve builds from the older checkout. Local npm 12 also returns a keyed `npm pack --json` result that `scripts/publish.mjs:182` cannot parse; the documented Node 22 publication workflow uses npm 10. I did not run a build, publication, bot interaction, service operation, credential flow, or live provider check. The repository's documented broader Windows fixture failures were not exercised in this focused run.
